These two appeals arise out of the judgment and order dated 15.09.2018 passed by learned Special Judge, (Under POCSO Act), Bhandara in Special (Child) Criminal Case No. 24/2016 and therefore,
they are being decided by this common judgment.
2. The appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 706/2018 is accused no.1 and the appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 139/2019 is accused no.2.

They have been held guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 376-D and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code ; under Sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as "the POCSO Act" for short) and under Sections 3(1)(xii) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as "the Atrocities Act" for short).

The informant (PW4) is the mother of the victim (PW1).
According to the prosecution, the incident of gang rape on the victim occurred on 22.04.2016.
The victim, at the time of the incident, was 14 years old.
The accused and the victim are resident of the same village.

It is the case of the prosecution that on 22.04.2016 between 10.00 and 11.00 am, one boy namely Aryan Ilpate, aged about 8 years, went to the house of the victim and told her that her friend Guddi had called her.
The victim accompanied Aryan to the house of Guddi.

When the victim reached near the house of accused no.2 Pravin, who was accompanied by Pappu @ Pramod, a juvenile in conflict with law and accused no.1 Vasanta, the accused persons caught hold her, gagged her mouth and took her in the house of accused no.2 Pravin.
Accused no.2 bolted the door of the house from inside.
The victim was taken to the inside room.
Accused removed the clothes of the victim.
Accused no.1 also removed all his clothes.

Accused no.2 and juvenile in conflict with law caught hold the hands of the victim to facilitate sexual intercourse on the victim by accused no.1.
Accused no.1 committed sexual intercourse with the victim.

12. It is undisputed that the report was lodged on 26.04.2016, whereas the alleged incident occurred on 22.04.2016 between 10.00 am and 11.00 am.

Before proceeding to appreciate the evidence of the victim and her mother with regard to the incident as well as explanation for lodging report after four days, it would be appropriate to consider the nature of the offence and perception of the society about the offence of rape.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Bharwada Bhoginbhai Hirjibhai .vs. State of Gujarat , reported at (1983) 3 SCC 217, has considered this issue in the context of Indian setting.

sentences.text: Paragraph 10 of the decision would be relevant.
It is extracted below :
"10. By and large these factors are not relevant to India, and the Indian conditions.

Without the fear of making too wide a statements or of overstating the case, it can be said that rarely will a girl or a woman in India make false allegations of sexual assault on account of any such factor as has been just enlisted.
The statement is generally true in the context of the urban as also rural Society.
It is also by and large true in the context of the sophisticated, not so sophisticated, and unsophisticated society.
Only very rarely can one conceivably come across an exception or two and that too possibly from amongst the urban elites.

Because: (1) A girl or a woman in the tradition bound non- permissive Society of India would be extremely reluctant even to admit that any incident which is likely to reflect on her chastity had ever occurred.

(2) She would be conscious of the danger of being ostracised by the Society or being looked down 11 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) by the Society including by her own family members, relatives,
friends and neighbours.
(3) She would have to brave the whole world.
(4) She would face the risk of losing the love and respect of her own husband and near relatives, and of her matrimonial home and happiness being shattered.
(5) If she is unmarried, she would apprehend that it would be difficult to secure an alliance with a suitable match from a respectable or an acceptable family.
(6) It would almost inevitably and almost invariably result in mental torture and suffering to herself.
(7) The fear of being taunted by others will always haunt her.

(8) She would feel extremely embarrassed in relating the incident to others being over powered by a feeling of shame on account of the upbringing in a tradition bound society where by and large sex is taboo.

13. It needs to be stated that in view of the above factors, the victims and their relatives are not too keen to bring the culprits to books.
And when in the face of these factors the crime is brought to light, there is a built-in assurance that the charge is genuine rather than fabricated.

In my view,
these 12 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) factors are required to be borne in mind while appreciating the evidence of the victim (PW1) and her mother (PW4).

14. The Hon'ble Apex Court in number of decisions has settled the legal position as to the delay in lodging report in sexual offences and consequences of such delay on the very core and crux of the evidence of the victim.
In this context, it would be appropriate to make useful reference to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in State of Rajasthan .vs. Om Prakash, reported at (2002) 5 SCC 745.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan .vs. Om Prakash, reported at (2002) 5 SCC 745
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the first information report in a criminal case is an extremely vital and valuable piece of evidence for the purpose of corroborating the oral evidence adduced at the trial.

The object of insisting upon prompt lodging of a report to the police in respect of commission of an offence is to obtain early information regarding the circumstances in which the crime was committed, the names of the culprits and the part played by them as well as the names of eye-witnesses present at the scene of occurrence.
It is held that the delay in lodging FIR quite often results in embellishment, which is a creature of an afterthought.

It is held that on account of delay, the report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, danger creeps in of the introduction of coloured version, exaggerated account or concocted story as a result of deliberation and consultation.
It is held that the Courts should adopt a sensitive approach in 13 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) dealing with the cases of child rape.
It is held that the delay put forth by the prosecution has to be appreciated keeping in mind all these factors.
15. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Himachal Pradesh .vs. Shree Kant Shekari,

It is a serious blow to her supreme honour and offends her self-esteem and dignity - it degrades and humiliates the victim and where the victim is a helpless innocent child or a minor, it leaves behind a traumatic experience.

A rapist not only causes physical injuries but more indelibly leaves a scar on the most cherished possession of a woman i.e. her dignity, honour,

sentences.text: Rape is not only a crime against the person of a woman, it is a crime against the entire society.
It destroys, as noted by this Court in Shri Bodhisattwa Gautam v. Miss Subhra Chakraborty (AIR 1996 SC 922), the entire psychology of a woman and pushes her into deep emotional crisis.

sentences.text: It is a crime against basic human rights, and is also violative of the victim's most cherished of the Fundamental Rights, namely, the Right to Life contained in Article 21 of the Constitution.
The Courts are, therefore, expected to deal with cases of sexual crime against women with utmost sensitivity.
Such cases need to be dealt with sternly and severely.
A socially sensitized judge, in our opinion, is a better statutory armour in cases of crime against women than long clauses of penal provisions, containing complex exceptions and provisos."
As far as the delay is concerned, it is held that the delay must be satisfactorily explained.
It is held that in any event, delay per se is not a mitigating circumstance for the accused when accusations of rape are involved.
It is held that delay in lodging FIR cannot be used as a ritualistic formula for discarding the prosecution case and doubting its authenticity.
It only puts the court on guard to search for and consider if any explanation has been offered for the delay.

Once it is offered,
the Court is to only see whether it is satisfactory or not.

It is held that in case if the prosecution fails to satisfactorily explain the delay and there is possibility of embellishment or exaggeration in the prosecution version on account of such delay, it is a relevant factor.
It is further held that on the other hand, satisfactory explanation of the delay is weighty enough to reject the plea of false implication or vulnerability of the prosecution case.

17. The Hon'ble Apex Court in State of Himachal Pradesh .vs. Sanjay Kumar alias Sunny, reported at (2017) 2 SCC 51 has analysed all the earlier decisions including the decision in the case of Shree Kant Shekari (supra) and with approval reiterated the same legal position.

In the backdrop of above stated legal position, with certainty, it can be said that in rape cases,
FIR is delayed due to many reasons such as, trauma caused to the victim and family, mental agony,
reputation of family and the future of the victim is at stake and also the societal pressure.
The delay must be explained satisfactorily.
The reasons for delay need proper appreciation and the same has to be decided as a question of fact on the basis of oral, documentary and circumstantial evidence.
In this case, it is the case of the prosecution that the victim was dragged inside the house by the accused.
It is not the defence of the accused that there was love affair between accused no.1 and the victim.
The victim has stated in her evidence that she was subjected to 17 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) sexual intercourse by accused no.1.
She has categorically stated that accused no.2 and the juvenile in conflict with law caught hold her hands and helped accused no.1 to complete the sexual intercourse.
The defence of enmity appears to be a half-hearted attempt.
Perusal of the statement of the accused recorded under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, would show that it has not been appropriately elaborated.
It was stated by the accused in their 313 statements that there are two political parties in the village and therefore, a false case is registered against them.

The victim, as per the case of the prosecution, disclosed the incident to her mother on 26.04.2016.
The report lodged by the victim is at Exh.37.
In her report, she has stated that on account of the threat extended by the accused, the report was not lodged immediately.
She has stated that on 26.04.2016, she narrated the incident for the first time to her mother and therefore, the mother brought her to the police station for lodging report.
The victim, as can be seen on the basis of documentary evidence, was hardly 14 years old at the time of the incident.
Accused no.1, on the date of the incident, was married.
He was 27 years old.
Accused no.2 was 20 years old and he was unmarried.
They both belong to 'Kunbi' caste, which is having dominant majority in the village.
The victim was dragged in the house in a broad daylight by the accused 18 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) persons.
This would show their dominance.
In ordinary circumstances, such a crime cannot be committed in a broad daylight and in this manner.
It is further pertinent to note that if the incident was disclosed to the mother on the first day of the incident, then there was no reason for the mother to cause delay in lodging the report.
Evidence of PW1 and PW4, as far as delay is concerned, is consistent.

19. An attempt has been made to suggest that the incident was reported to the police on the date of the incident itself and police had come to the village and rescued the victim from the house of accused no.2.
It is evident that such a statement was made by PW4 before the police.
However, at the time of her evidence, she did not depose about the same in her evidence.
She was confronted with this statement.
It has been proved.
This statement is sought to be relied upon to doubt the very reason for delayed lodging of the FIR.
In my view, this fact cannot be read in isolation.
For this purpose, the evidence on record is required to be considered in its entirety.

If the police had visited the village on the date of the incident, then there ought to have been ample documentary evidence in the form of entry in the station diary as to the visit of the police to the village and subsequent entry with regard to the result of the said visit.

In my view, in order to fortify this contention, it was expected on the part of learned advocate for the accused to question the Investigating Officer or the police officer about it at the time of his evidence.
Learned 19 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) advocate could have called upon the police officer to produce the relevant record.
As far as evidence of the victim is concerned, she is silent about visit of the police to the village on the date of the incident.

In my view,
therefore, this statement has to be properly appreciated keeping in mind the evidence of PW4 in its entirety.
Learned Judge has dealt with this aspect.
The reasons recorded by the learned Judge, in my view, are just and proper.
In this case, failure on the part of the victim to disclose the incident to PW4 might be her decision on account of the threat extended to her.
PW4 mother, therefore, could not control the thought process of the victim in this regard.
It is evident that when the victim disclosed the incident on the 4 th day, she immediately took the victim to the police station.
It has been proved that except for the threat of dire consequences extended by the accused, there was no other reason for the informant to lodge the report after four days of the incident.
In the set up of Indian society, it cannot be said that this conduct was inconsistent or highly objectionable.
It was, in my view, but natural to take proper precautions to safeguard the future of the girl and the pride and prestige of the family.

This would now take me to the evidence of the prosecution.
The victim (PW1) in her evidence has placed on record the first hand account of the incident.
The victim in a rape case is placed on a higher pedestal than an injured witness.
She cannot be treated as an accomplice.
Similarly, the standard of corroboration in the case of an accomplice cannot be insisted upon 20 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) in the case of the victim of a rape case.
She has deposed that when she was going to the house of her friend Guddi, accused nos.1 and 2 and juvenile in conflict with law caught hold of her and carried her inside the house of accused no.2.
She has narrated the incident in detail.
She has stated that accused no.2 and juvenile in conflict with law caught hold of her hands and accused no.1 committed rape on her.
She has stated that when her mother came and gave a call by banging on the door, her mouth was tied with a handkerchief by the accused.
She has further stated that a threat to kill her was given in case the incident was disclosed to anyone.
The victim, in her evidence, has stated that her birth date is 06.06.2002.
A certified copy of the Birth Certificate, issued by the Gram Panchayat is at Exh.39.
The accused persons have not challenged either the oral evidence of the victim or this documentary evidence.
Exh.39 was issued by a public authority, which is supposed to maintain such records.
The victim was subjected to searching and gruelling cross-examination.
Perusal of her cross-examination would show that not a single admission has been brought on record to dent her evidence or doubt her credibility.
She has denied the suggestion that the accused have been falsely implicated on account of village political rivalry.
21. PW4 is the mother of the victim.
In her evidence, she has stated that boy Aryan came to her and told her that the accused caught hold the victim and dragged her in the house.
It needs to be stated at this stage that boy 21 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) Aryan
, at the time of the incident, was 10 years old.
He was called as witness by the prosecution.

However, the learned Judge, on the basis of the inquiry to decide the competence of this witness, found that he was not in a position to understand the importance of oath and therefore, his evidence could not be recorded.
PW4 has stated that when she went to the house of accused no.2, she found that the door was closed from inside.
She gave calls to her daughter.
The door was opened by accused no.2 and on opening the door, he told that it is not the house of prostitute.
She was not allowed to enter the house.
However, she gained entry in the house and made an inquiry with accused no.2 and the juvenile in conflict with law.
They told her that her daughter was not in their house.
However, she found chappals of her daughter.
On inquiry with accused no.2 about the chappals, accused no.2 told that the chappals belonged to his mother.
PW4 identified the pair of chappals and carried the same to her house.
PW1-victim has stated that after hearing shouts of her mother, accused no.1 tied her mouth with handkerchief and carried her to dhaba, which is a floor of the house constructed with bamboo.
Perusal of cross- examination of PW4 would show that her evidence was consistent with the evidence of the victim.
On minute perusal of the evidence of PW1 and PW4, I am satisfied that their evidence is worthy of credence.
Evidence of PW4 has not been shaken at all in the cross-examination.
I do not see any reason to discard and disbelieve the first hand account of the incident narrated by the victim.
In case of incident of rape, unless it happens in public view, there is no 22 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) possibility of any independent witness.
In such an incident, majority of the witnesses are the family members to whom the victim later on confides and narrates the incident.
The victim and the mother, in ordinary circumstances, for trifle reasons which have been suggested in the cross-examination, would not have taken such a risk.
The mother would not have even thought of putting the future and career of her daughter in jeopardy.

Apart from putting the future and career of the victim in jeopardy, the Pravin S/O. Gangaram Rehpade(In ... vs State Of Maharashtra Thr. P.S.O., P.S. ... on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184310261/
10 incident would have defamed and lowered down the pride and prestige of the family in the village.
In my view, therefore, the evidence of PW1 and PW4 cannot be discarded and disbelieved.
22. The evidence relied upon by the prosecution to seek corroboration to the version of the victim is the evidence of Medical Officers PW6 and PW8.
Perusal of their evidence would show that both the Medical officers have stated that examination of the victim by them revealed that she was subjected to sexual intercourse.
It is found that in the report to police, external injuries sustained by the victim were not mentioned.
The victim for the first time before the Court has deposed about those injuries.
In my view, merely because of failure of the victim to mention those injuries in the report, it cannot be concluded that she had not sustained the injuries.
In my view, for this purpose, the evidence of Medical Officers is required to be properly appreciated.
PW6 Dr. Meena Sonwane, on 27.04.2016, examined the victim.
She has deposed that the victim had narrated the history of assault on her by three persons, namely Vasanta, Pappu and Pravin on 22.04.2016 at about 10.00 a.m. at village Dighori/Amgaon.

As far as external injuries are concerned,
she found the following injuries on the body of the victim :
i] Abrasion over left forearm, middle 1/3rd extensor surface, size 1 cm, brownish black colour.
ii] Bruise over left forearm, middle 1/3rd, flexor aspect, 4 x 1/2 cm, brownish black colour.
iii] Four abrasions over extensor surface, left forearm, lower 1/3rd, approximately 1/2 cm, brownish black colour.

iv] Abrasion over right side's lateral surface thigh, 1 cm,
brownish black.
On clinical examination of the victim, she found that her hymen was torn.
PW6 has stated in an answer to the query report received from the police that the injuries were more than 48 hours old.
She has stated that on the basis of the examination, she opined that there was sexual assault on the victim.
She has admitted that she was not 100% sure about it and therefore, the victim was referred to Dr. Snehal Bandebuche, a Gynaecologist (PW8).
PW6 has stated that the injuries on the person of the victim could be caused by nails.
She has admitted in her cross-examination that she has not specifically mentioned the approximate time of tear of hymen.
She has also admitted that she has not recorded in her report the kind of hymen torn.

11 24.
PW8 is Dr. Shehal Bandebuche.
She has stated that on 27.04.2016, she examined the victim girl.
The victim girl was referred to her by Dr. Sonawane for gynec opinion/expert opinion.
She has stated that the victim confirmed the history of assault before her.
She has stated that on internal examination, she found genital hymen was not intact.
The vagina admitted tip of finger.
She has stated that on the basis of her examination she formed the opinion that there was a possibility of sexual intercourse with the victim.
She has admitted that in the case of forcible penetrative intercourse there must be evidence of injury to the genital part.
In my view, this admission is of no help to the accused.
She has stated that the victim's genital hymen was not intact.
In short, she confirmed the observations of Dr. Sonawane (PW6) that the hymen was torn.
PW6 Dr. Sonawane has admitted that tear of hymen was possible while cycling or doing heavy exercise.
In my view, this admission has to be read in the context of the first hand account of the incident of rape narrated by the victim.
The victim has stated that accused no.1 committed forcible sexual intercourse with her.
The external injuries, which were more than 48 hours old, are the confirmation that the victim was subjected to forcible sexual intercourse.
The victim was alone.
She was over powered by accused and sexual intercourse was committed by accused no.1.
In my view, therefore, the evidence of the Medical Officers is sufficient to corroborate the evidence of the victim.
Evidence of the Medical Officers (PW6 and PW8) lends an assurance to the evidence of the victim (PW1) and her mother (PW4) 25 APEAL 706.18+1 (J) as to the incident of rape.
I do not see any reason to discard and disbelieve the evidence of the Medical Officers.
25. The prosecution has proved that the victim, on the date of the incident, was 14 years old.
The victim was a "child" as understood by Section 2(d) of the POCSO Act.
Three persons were involved in commission of the offence of rape.

Learned Judge has convicted and sentenced the accused for the above offences.

Gond' caste, which is a Scheduled Tribe.

caste.
Learned Judge found that the offence under the Atrocities Act was proved against the accused.

26. On re-appreciation of the evidence, I am satisfied that the learned Special Judge has not committed any mistake while appreciating the evidence as well as recording a finding as to the offences proved against the accused persons.
In view of this, I do not see any substance in the appeal.
The Criminal Appeal is accordingly dismissed.
